questions.question: Which 1958 novel by Chinua Achebe is considered the founding work of modern African literature in English?
questions.explanation: "Things Fall Apart" (1958) depicted Igbo society from within and challenged colonial portrayals of Africa, founding modern African literature in English.

questions.question: What radical linguistic decision did Ngugi wa Thiong'o make?
options: He stopped writing in English and switched to his native Gikuyu
questions.explanation: Ngugi argued that African literature should be written in African languages and switched from English to Gikuyu - an act of decolonizing the mind.

questions.question: What is "the danger of a single story", according to Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie?
options: Repeated exposure to only one narrative about a people creates stereotypes
Reading only one book per year
Novels with a single plot line
questions.explanation: In her 2009 TED Talk, Adichie warned that hearing only one story about a group or place produces incomplete, stereotyped understanding.

questions.question: What historical conflict is the backdrop of Adichie's "Half of a Yellow Sun" (2006)?
questions.explanation: "Half of a Yellow Sun" is set during the Nigerian Civil War of 1967-1970, when Biafra attempted to secede from Nigeria.

questions.question: Why did Achebe choose to write in English rather than Igbo?
options: He wanted to reach a global audience and reshape the language to carry African experience
Igbo had no words for stories
questions.explanation: Achebe deliberately used English - enriched with Igbo proverbs and rhythms - to tell African stories to the world, in contrast to Ngugi's position.
